faqs.question: What is the Xevo G3 QTof used for?
faqs.answer: It's a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer for both detailed characterization and accurate quantitation, covering challenging small molecules through to complex biotherapeutics on one system.

faqs.question: What mass range does the Xevo G3 QTof cover?
faqs.answer: The calibration range extends to m/z 16,000, which is what brings complex biologics into scope alongside small molecule work.

faqs.question: What is StepWave XS?
faqs.answer: An ion transmission technology that efficiently transmits low mass, labile species, increasing compound coverage and analytical fidelity for analytes that are otherwise easily lost.

faqs.question: What dynamic range does the system offer?
faqs.answer: Up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to a 4× increase in in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted and screening experiments.

faqs.question: What is the difference between linear and in-spectrum dynamic range?
faqs.answer: Linear dynamic range describes the concentration span over which a known analyte quantifies reliably. In-spectrum dynamic range describes how large an abundance difference can be resolved within a single spectrum, which matters when low-abundance components sit alongside high-abundance ones.

faqs.question: Can one instrument really handle both qualitative and quantitative work?
faqs.answer: That's the design intent — Waters positions it as a flexible multifunctional instrument delivering high-quality quantitative and qualitative data sets, maximizing system usage across both workflow types.

faqs.question: What is waters_connect?
faqs.answer: An informatics ecosystem harmonizing workflows across development, manufacturing, and QC, offering compliance-ready workflows with security-controlled access, full data traceability, and networked deployment.

faqs.question: How does the system support the transition from development to QC?
faqs.answer: Biomolecules and processes are characterized on the Xevo G3 QTof first, then transition to dedicated attribute monitoring assays either on the same system or on the BioAccord System with ACQUITY Premier, with waters_connect carrying the workflow.

faqs.question: What software controls the instrument?
faqs.answer: MassLynx for acquiring, analyzing, managing, and sharing nominal and exact mass MS and MS/MS data, and the waters_connect ecosystem for connected, compliance-ready workflows.

faqs.question: How robust is the instrument for high-throughput use?
faqs.answer: Updated ion optics design and optimized ion beam conditioning are engineered specifically to deliver consistent robustness and reproducibility, maintaining performance and productivity over a longer time period.

faqs.question: Which LC systems pair with the Xevo G3 QTof?
faqs.answer: Waters pairs it with ACQUITY Premier in its own materials, and it has been applied with ACQUITY UPLC I-Class PLUS and M-Class in published application work.

longForm.heroHook: Characterize a biotherapeutic and quantify a small molecule impurity. Same instrument, same week.
longForm.heroLead: Most labs end up splitting the work: a high-resolution instrument for characterization, a separate one for quantitation, each idle while the other runs. Xevo G3 QTof is built to carry both, which is why Waters calls it an analytical workhorse rather than a specialist. The range is real. An m/z 16,000 calibration range with tailored informatics handles complex biologics; updated ion optics and detection maximize transmission and dynamic range for challenging small molecules. StepWave XS efficiently transmits low mass, labile species — the ones that go missing on instruments not built to carry them. On the quantitative side, core technology updates deliver up to 5 orders of linear dynamic range for targeted analysis, and up to 4× more in-spectrum dynamic range for untargeted screening in complex matrices. The waters_connect ecosystem then carries those workflows from development through manufacturing into QC, with security-controlled access and full data traceability.

sections.title: Reliability Across a Full Campaign
sections.description: Peak sensitivity on a clean standard tells you what an instrument can do once. A quantitative lab needs to know what it does on injection 900, in a matrix that has been depositing residue since injection one.
body: Waters answered that specifically. A mycotoxin study in wheat flour — a matrix they explicitly name as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation — ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use.
Peak area RSD held between 3 and 8% across that campaign, meaning the instrument's response didn't drift meaningfully as the source accumulated matrix.
Proven ion guide technology is what Waters credits for maintaining uptime as standard, and the Xevo family's inherent robustness is the design lineage behind it.

The detector data carries real provenance rather than being a general claim: fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers launched between 2006 and 2022 require a detector replacement on an annual basis, from their own service history.

A low noise, off-axis photomultiplier is the design choice behind that longevity — off-axis geometry keeps neutrals and photons off the detector surface, which is what shortens detector life on in-line designs.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: Xevo TQ-S micro product information: sensitivity, uptime record, source flexibility, and software options.
body: Xevo TQ-S micro is a compact tandem quadrupole mass spectrometer from the inherently robust Xevo family, providing superior performance per square inch alongside exceptional analytical flexibility.
Waters positions it as a laboratory workhorse, offering best value performance per square inch of bench space with unrivalled flexibility to meet changing, growing, or unexpected analytical demands.

Waters' internal global service data shows customers using the instrument will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after — with planned scheduled Performance Maintenance visits still recommended for trouble-free operation.

A mycotoxin study in wheat flour, a complex matrix Waters identifies as one that can contaminate LC-MS instrumentation, showed consistent performance across 5 days of continuous use and 1,000 injections at 5–9% RSD for peak areas.
Sensitivity is rated ★★★ on Waters' five-point scale — above Xevo TQ-S cronos (★★), below TQ-XS (★★★★) and TQ Absolute XR (★★★★★).
Mass range is 2 to 2048 m/z, and MRM speed is 555 MRM/sec, matching cronos and exceeding both TQ-XS and TQ Absolute XR at 500 MRM/sec.
Ion source transfer optics use StepWave, the same as cronos.
Eight ion sources are compatible: APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI as standard, ionKey, nanoflow, and UniSpray — three more than cronos, adding APGC, ionKey, and nanoflow.
Six acquisition modes are supported: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, MRM, and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).
Detection uses a low noise, off-axis, long life photomultiplier; fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement.
Chromatographic compatibility covers ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
Dimensions are 35.6 x 60 x 93 cm — identical to cronos, and 2–3× narrower than other instruments in its class.
Electricity consumption and associated heat production are up to 34% lower than other instruments in its class.
Two software platforms are available: waters_connect for Quantitation and MassLynx v4.2, with MassLynx security supported.
waters_connect includes Exception Focused Review (XFR), which Waters states can save up to 50% of data review time.
Third-party interfaces include LIMS and the MassLynx SkyLine interface.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.
Note that ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, ASAP, ESCi, ionKey, and nanoflow are marked by Waters as not available with waters_connect.

sections.title: Uptime and Reliability Under Load
sections.description: Instrument downtime in a quantitative lab is rarely just the repair. It's the requalification afterwards, the backlog that built during it, and the questions about whether data either side of the fault is comparable.
body: Waters makes a specific, checkable claim: customers using the Xevo TQ-S micro will on average not need an unplanned service visit during the warranty period and for 3 years after, sourced to their internal global service data on unplanned visits.

Their own caveat travels with it and matters — planned visits for regular scheduled Performance Maintenance are recommended to ensure trouble-free operation. The claim is about unplanned interruptions, not maintenance-free running.
Performance under matrix load is separately evidenced. The mycotoxin study in wheat flour ran 1,000 injections across 5 days of continuous use, holding peak area RSD between 5 and 9%.

Worth noting for anyone comparing directly: Xevo TQ-S cronos returned 3–8% RSD on the equivalent study. TQ-S micro's advantage over cronos sits in sensitivity, source range, and this uptime record rather than in campaign precision.

Detector longevity carries the same provenance as across the Xevo TQ line — fewer than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupoles launched between 2006 and 2022 require an annual detector replacement. The off-axis photomultiplier geometry is the design reason: keeping neutrals and photons off the detector surface is what extends life relative to in-line arrangements.

body: Coupled with ACQUITY UPLC, Xevo TQ-XS is built for routine quantitative workflows that need superior sensitivity, adaptability, and flexibility as analytical demands evolve.

StepWave XS ion source transfer optics sit specifically at this tier, positioned between the standard StepWave design on the TQ-S cronos and TQ-S micro, and the StepWave XR optics used on TQ Absolute XR.
Mass range covers 2 to 2048 m/z, with MRM speed reaching 500 transitions per second, supported by a low-noise, off-axis, long-life photomultiplier detector.
Six acquisition modes are available: full scan, product scan, precursor ion scan, constant neutral loss scan, multiple reaction monitoring (MRM), and simultaneous full scan and MRM (RADAR).

Ion source compatibility spans APCI, APGC, ASAP, ESCi, ESI, ionKey, Nanoflow, and UniSpray, matched to a chromatographic configuration compatibility list including ACQUITY Premier, ACQUITY UPC2, ACQUITY UPLC, ACQUITY UPLC M-Class, and APGC.
In a direct vancomycin comparison, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS came in more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S.
A representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, demonstrates the sensitivity and selectivity available at this tier.

Detector reliability runs high across the installed base, with less than 1% of Waters' tandem quadrupole mass spectrometers requiring a detector replacement annually, based on internal service data from units launched between 2006 and 2022.
Software options include MassLynx v4.2 and waters_connect for Quantitation, both supporting LIMS interfaces and MassLynx SkyLine interfaces, with MassLynx security included as standard.
Regulatory approval marks include CE, CB, NRTL (Canada/USA), and RCM.

sections.title: Sensitivity Where It Matters Most
sections.description: A sensitivity claim means more with a direct comparison behind it than a general performance statement alone.
body: For vancomycin, average analyte area counts on Xevo TQ-XS measured more than 10 times higher than on Xevo TQ-S, a direct, quantified sensitivity gain rather than an approximate improvement.

On the low-concentration end, a representative liraglutide LLOQ chromatogram at 0.5 ng/mL, extracted from plasma, shows both the sensitivity and the selectivity available at this concentration, relevant for bioanalytical work operating near a method's detection limit.

Behind both results sits the StepWave XS ion source transfer optics, purpose-built for this sensitivity tier within the Xevo TQ family, positioned above the standard StepWave design and below the StepWave XR optics on TQ Absolute XR.

Set against what the analysis needs: confidence at trace-level concentrations comes from the demonstrated 0.5 ng/mL LLOQ performance on liraglutide; measurable sensitivity gains over standard TQ systems come from the >10x area counts versus Xevo TQ-S on vancomycin; reliable detection at the needed sensitivity tier comes from the purpose-built StepWave XS optics; and high-throughput analysis without losing sensitivity comes from the 500 MRM/sec speed.
